logs.title: Minutes, Ring Three
logs.text:
Item 1: the heating. Item 2: the heating. Item 3: whether items 1 and 2 are the same item.
Motion carried, 14 to 14, by the casting vote of the heating.
Item 4: the Snap. Deferred to next week.
Item 4 has been deferred for forty years.

logs.title: Ticket No. 0001
logs.text:
Ticket 0001 was issued today. We have kept every ticket since.
612,000 so far, in a warehouse we call Receipts. The warehouse is now bigger than the dock.
We can't throw them out. Somebody might want to check.

logs.title: Second Notice
logs.text:
To whoever owns this rock now: the rent is due. To whoever owned it before: the rent was due.
To whoever owns it next: tell them the rent is due.
Signed, the landlord, who is also the tenant, who is also, now we think of it, the rock.

logs.title: Spoke Ferry Seven
logs.text:
Spoke Ferry Seven departs on the hour. Spoke Ferry Seven has departed on the hour for forty years.
Spoke Ferry Seven has not arrived.
I will raise it at the next meeting.
The next meeting is on the hour.

logs.title: Day 19
logs.text:
Four families in a three-person flat. Day nineteen. We have made a rota for the bathroom, and a rota for the rota.
Nobody has killed anybody. I want that noted.
I want a medal.

logs.title: Candle count
logs.text:
Candle count at the vigil: sixty-one thousand and four. I counted. Somebody had to.
One window was dark. I flew past it. Then I turned round, lit mine, and put it in the window.
For the record, I do not know who lived there. I have asked the whole ring. Nobody does.

logs.title: Greeting, in full
logs.text:
Our new engineer said hello on Monday. He finished on Tuesday.
By Wednesday we had decided he was the best conversationalist on the ship.
He fixed the reactor on Thursday. Nobody saw. It ran better by Friday.
I think he meant to.

logs.title: The Count
logs.text:
Found a stone with a column of marks. Slate says they are a count. I asked, a count of what. He said, 'Not yet.'
I asked, how many. He said, 'Not enough.'
That night I dreamed in tallies. I haven't mentioned it. Slate hasn't asked.

logs.title: Notice board
logs.text:
Blast notice, east face. 'Imminent.' Posted: day one of the Quarry. Nobody has complained.
The board holds eleven thousand notices. Most say 'imminent'. A few say 'overdue'. One says 'please'.
The one that says 'please' is on top.

logs.title: Delivery slot
logs.text:
Delivery slot for block 41: pending. Delivery slot for block 42: pending.
We have been parked at the gate for forty years. The crew say it is fine. The crew are very calm.
I am less calm. I keep a little tally of my calm. It is going down.

logs.title: Night shift
logs.text:
Lights out in the yard at nine. Slate never turns his lamp off. Asked why.
'So the stones can see me,' he said.
I laughed. He looked at me for a very long minute. I turned my lamp on too.

logs.title: Plumb line
logs.text:
Surveyor's note, the Arch: plumb to within a hair. A hair of what, I couldn't say. It is the best thing anyone has built, and it has no door in it.
I asked my Basalt mate why. 'Because it was not finished,' he said.
I asked what was missing. 'You will know,' he said.
I do not.

logs.title: Thermostat
logs.text:
Day 3: someone turned the thermostat down to 22 for the Human. The whole deck is in coats.
Day 4: someone turned it down to 18 for the Human. The whole deck is in a pile.
Day 5: the Human has moved into the engine room. We are all friends now.

logs.title: Cold Night
logs.text:
I did it. I sat in the cold room for the whole night. Twenty degrees. My toes are still there; I counted.
The others gave me a medal, which is a red rag.
I am keeping it forever. I am going to put it in my forge. It will burn.

logs.title: Rent in light
logs.text:
The Forge pays rent in light. This is not a metaphor.
The Lumen measure the Forge's glow each week and bill by the lumen.
The Forge has been glowing a bit dim. Cinder says it is because they are tired.
The Lumen say 'tired' is not a unit.

logs.title: Slag manifest
logs.text:
Cargo: 40 tonnes slag, hot. 40 tonnes slag, warm. 40 tonnes slag, formerly hot.
We have run out of words for temperature. We are now using adjectives.
The last batch is described as 'emotional'.

logs.title: The Coal
logs.text:
The Coal is dimmer than last year. I measured. Don't tell Cinder.
Nobody wants to say it. The Coal is going out, a hair at a time, and the Forge is built on it.
We have planned for everything but that. We will have to learn to be cold.
I have started practising. I hate it.

logs.title: To the cold ones
logs.text:
To whoever is reading this, who is probably cold: we made you a blanket.
We do not know what temperature you like. We made it warm. We made it very warm.
If it is too warm, sorry. If it is not warm enough, well, we never understood you either.
Love, the Forge.

logs.title: Receipt for a receipt
logs.text:
Received: one receipt, for one receipt.
Received: one receipt, for the receipt of the receipt.
The Bazaar runs on these. I do not understand how, but nothing has ever gone missing.
I tried to steal something. I got a receipt.

logs.title: Free sample
logs.text:
Entry to the Bazaar is free. Exit is 12 credits.
I have been inside nine weeks. The exit fee has doubled. I am now paying rent on my own lungs.
I love it here. I will never leave. I cannot afford to.

logs.title: Closing sale
logs.text:
Day 1 of the closing sale. Everything must go.
Day 90 of the closing sale. Everything must go.
Day 400. Everything has gone except the till and us.
The till is the only thing not for sale. We have decided that is the point.

logs.title: Underwriting note
logs.text:
Policy 4,417: the ship was insured against fire, flood, falling, and falling in a flood on fire.
She sank. She was fine; it was the harbour that went.
The claim was rejected on the grounds that 'the harbour' was not listed. I have filed this as a lesson in careful reading, and sent myself a bill.

logs.title: Dead quiet
logs.text:
The hour of fixed prices again. I have nothing to say. I have to say that I have nothing to say.
It is the loudest hour of the day. The hush rings.
I wrote down what I would have said. It was a joke about a discount. I hope somebody reads it.

logs.title: Dismissal
logs.text:
Dismissed from the Brokers' Guild: Tuppence, for excessive candour. Hearing at noon.
She asked what that meant. They said, 'You told the buyer the price was fair.'
She asked, 'Was it?' They said, 'That is not the point.'
I am not going to say what I think. But I have written it down, here.

logs.title: Quarter shares
logs.text:
Payday: 40 credits, split four ways. Ten each. Nobody asked for different.
The human on the next dock got a bonus and was unhappy. We got no bonus and were not.
I think I understand why. I think we have more than they do.

logs.title: Seven days alone
logs.text:
Day 1. This one is alone.
Day 3. This one is still alone.
Day 5. This one talks to the stove. The stove does not tick back.
Day 7. A ship came. It smelled like home. This one will go to them.

logs.title: The song
logs.text:
The mother-song was in the air when we hatched. Forty years it has not played.
We tried to build our own. It was not right. The ones who know the real one are old now.
We record them every week. We are afraid of the day we record the last.

logs.title: Form 9
logs.text:
Day 3. Four arms. Two contracts. I have written to the Office.
Day 5. The Office replied: 'Resolve.'
Day 6. I am sharing my sandwich with the knot. It is a sandwich for four.
I think I understand something. I cannot say what.

logs.title: Brood room
logs.text:
Hatchlings ate the cheese. Hatchlings ate the other cheese. Hatchlings ate the sign that said NO CHEESE.
We are not angry. We are very proud. They are loud and wonderful and we are tired.
Somebody is going to have to clean the ceiling.

logs.title: A place for her
logs.text:
Knot Seven has three. We still lay four places at table.
Her bowl is there. Her jacket is on the chair.
New crews ask who the fourth is. We say, 'She is out.'
It is true, in the way things are.

logs.title: Bucket inventory
logs.text:
Buckets, galley: 4. Buckets, bridge: 4. Buckets, buckets: 11.
The Chief asked what the last were for. I said, 'In case we need to carry the others.'
He said it was the most sensible thing he had heard all year.
We are now at 19 buckets and rising.

logs.title: Three a.m.
logs.text:
Fire alarm, 3 a.m. False. Fire alarm, 3:10. False. Fire alarm, 3:20. Real.
The crew arrived in slippers. Nobody had time for shoes.
The fire went out in six minutes. We made tea. The tea was awful.
Best night of the year.

logs.title: Wages, unpaid
logs.text:
Wet Watch wages, unpaid since the Snap: 41 years, 6 months, 11 days.
The Watch has been asked to accept payment. The Watch has declined, four times.
Reason given: 'It would make it a job.'
I have not told them it is a job. I have not told them they are very good at it.

logs.title: Dry week
logs.text:
Dry week on the ship. The Mire mate has been moping. His hands have gone grey.
He says, 'It is not the dry. It is the lack of company.'
I gave him a bucket. He has named it.
He says the bucket is a good listener.

logs.title: Fog log
logs.text:
Visibility: nil. Hearing: voices, three. Position: not where we left it.
Order to the crew: do not follow the voices. Reason: they are coming from inside.
Revised order: do not answer the voices. They know us well enough already.

logs.title: Manifest
logs.text:
Cargo: 2 tonnes of dry goods. 4 tonnes of wet goods. 1 tonne of goods the Mire call 'moist'.
It is the only cargo I have carried that was happier on arrival than on departure.
I do not know what to make of that. The Mire do not seem surprised.

logs.title: The good smell
logs.text:
Visited the Grove for the study. The crew complained of the smell for a day, then stopped.
The air does something to you. I slept nine hours. I have not slept nine hours since I was a child.
I have requested a transfer to the Grove. The Lumen has said I am 'too relaxed for the study'.

logs.title: Consent form
logs.text:
Specimen consent form, Version 1: 'May we take a sample?'
Version 2: 'May we take a sample, please?' Version 3: 'May we?'
Version 4: a drawing of a jar, a question mark and a flower.
The specimen signed Version 4. I have never been so moved by paperwork.

logs.title: Gone fishing
logs.text:
Crew left on Friday. Back by Monday. The ship had moss by Sunday.
By Tuesday the moss had ferns. By Wednesday the ferns had an opinion.
The note on the door says: GONE FISHING. BACK WHEN THE FERNS SAY.

logs.title: Minutes, the tulip
logs.text:
Council in session: day 3. Item: the tulip.
Positions: 'Tulip.' 'Not Tulip.' 'Tulip, but nicely.'
I have been asked to take minutes. I am told the minutes will take longer than the meeting.
The tulip is very patient.

logs.title: Spore storm
logs.text:
Storm warning: the dust is saying something. Everyone on deck hears it. Nobody agrees what.
I wrote down my version. It says 'Come home.' I do not have a home.
I put the pad in the airlock so that I will not read it again.

logs.title: Dry corridor
logs.text:
Someone put a dryer in the Grove's corridor. It was a good dryer. It dried the corridor.
It also dried everything in the corridor, including the Sporeling who was in it.
She is fine. She is the colour of a wafer. We have asked her to sit in the wet room until she remembers her name.

logs.title: About Dennis
logs.text:
Lost the left arm to a reactor, a sunrise, and a man named Dennis.
The reactor I understand. The sunrise was unlucky. But Dennis I will never forgive.
I keep the arm in a jar. I talk to it. It talks back, when it isn't busy.

logs.title: Best Accident
logs.text:
Contest night. First place: the fellow who fell into a drydock and came out as a tug.
Second place: the woman struck by lightning twice, in the same place, at the same hour.
Third place: me. I only got blown off a gantry.
I am working on a better one.

logs.title: Ion day
logs.text:
Ion storm at noon. Everyone on the Row stood still with their eyes shut and their arms in.
Three seconds after it hit we all came back and said 'Again?' as one.
I don't know why we laugh. We lose three seconds of our lives each time, and each time it is the best three seconds.
Nobody has noticed they are gone.

logs.title: Warrant
logs.text:
Warrant: one arm, stolen. One Gauntling, attached.
The Clan was asked to explain how an arm can be stolen from the person it is attached to.
The Clan's reply: 'We have a form for that.' They did. It was a form for returning an arm.
The arm refused to sign.

logs.title: Splice, day one
logs.text:
A torso on a cart arrived at the yard today and asked for a leg. I gave it a leg. It asked for another. I gave it another.
It asked for a head. I said, 'You have one.' It said, 'A better one.'
I believe this is how we all began. I gave it a hat.

logs.title: Final notice
logs.text:
Notice to the owners of this vessel: you are three payments behind.
Notice 2: you are four payments behind. Notice 3: you are still alive, but the ship has stopped.
Notice 4: the ship is no longer yours. It never was. It belongs to whoever is nearest. Congratulations.
Signed, the bank.

logs.title: Flat
logs.text:
The apprentice hummed flat in Hall 3. The pylons cracked. The Cantor said nothing.
The apprentice stood there an hour with her core flickering. At last the Cantor said, 'Do it again.' She did, still flat. 'Again.' Flat. 'Again.'
On the ninth try it was a different kind of flat. The Cantor said, 'That one is yours.'

logs.title: Elegy, 112 bars
logs.text:
Funeral for Spire 9. 112 bars. The score has no flat notes. We sang it flawless.
Afterwards the apprentice, Glint, was found in the lane humming one bar over and over. A single flat.
She said, 'I put one in for the Spire.' Nobody told her off.

logs.title: Unit 114
logs.text:
Audit, Choir. Unit 114 would not give her serial number. She hummed it instead.
I asked what it meant. She hummed, 'It means my name.' I wrote 'Unit 114 (insubordinate)'.
Then I crossed it out. I wrote 'Opal'.
I do not know where I got the name.

logs.title: The Eleven
logs.text:
We gather for the Eleven each year. We do not know why. We do not know who taught it to us.
I asked an elder. She hummed, 'It was in the glass when we were grown.'
If it was in the glass, someone sang it to the glass. I should like to know who.

logs.title: Garden notes
logs.text:
Day 4: asked the spire for a shard. It said no.
Day 5: asked again. It said no, more kindly.
Day 6: I sat. I did not ask. I sang it the song my mother sang.
Day 7: a shard on my palm. I do not think it was a trade.

logs.title: Resting our voices
logs.text:
Once a year the Choir rests its voices. All of them. For a day.
The whole station goes quiet. The Prismatics stand in rows, glowing, listening to the lack.
I asked what they hear. One hummed: 'Everything that was under it.'

logs.title: Sorry
logs.text:
Apologies logged this week by the crew of the Apology: 614.
For the door: 211. For the chair: 140. For the ceiling: 93. For the noise: 77. For existing: 14.
The captain says we will stop when we stop being too big. The captain is ten feet nine.

logs.title: Soup, day 3
logs.text:
Soup on the stove: 400 litres. Soup eaten: 380. Soup remaining: 20.
This has been judged a failure of planning. We have made another 400.
The galley is now a soup. It has a tide.

logs.title: No route
logs.text:
Route requested: none. Route issued: none. Route needed: ours.
We have been asked where we are going. We said: toward.
The marshal wrote 'toward' in the box. She underlined it. She is a kind woman.

logs.title: Name-board
logs.text:
I walked the length of the Provision today. Every door has a name. Every name is a cousin.
At the last door was mine. I did not know she had been here.
I took the plaque. I left a biscuit.

logs.title: Governor
logs.text:
Governor failed, 04:10. Speed increasing, 04:11. Speed increasing, 04:12.
I have asked the crew to remain calm. They are always calm.
I would like to apologise to the Convoy, in advance, for what we are about to do to it.

logs.title: Lashing
logs.text:
The lashing was today. Two sterns, one cable, a hundred and forty tonnes of knot.
The groom cried so hard the cable rang. The bride cried so hard it rang back.
Afterwards they held each other for an hour, and the barges leaned together, and the whole Convoy swayed. Nobody mentioned the weather.
